info.title: Margaya API
info.description: Margaya Project Management API - Manage projects, tasks, labels, and more

isFinal.description: True exactly when the group is completed or cancelled.

ColumnGroup.description: What the column means: backlog, unstarted (not started), started, completed, cancelled, or triage (reserved for intake). Aggregations order groups in that sequence, with triage first.

descriptionDeferred.description: True when the list omits a large description; load the task detail or description pages to read it. Do not replace stored text with this null summary.

priority.description: One of: no-priority, low, medium, high, urgent.

isMilestone.description: True when the task marks one date; the timeline draws it on its due date. Set it with PUT /task/milestone/{id}.

archivedAt.description: When the task was archived; null while it is not. An archived task keeps its column (status).

createdBy.description: The user who created the task; null for tasks made by integrations or whose creator was deleted.

userId.description: The first assignee, or null.

assigneeIds.description: Every assignee's user id, first assignee first.

assignees.description: Every assignee, first assignee first. Always complete on every page and related page.

cycleId.description: The cycle the task is planned in, or null. Always null while the project's cycles feature is off.

estimatePointId.description: Point of the project's active estimate system, or null. Resolve its value with GET /estimate/{projectId}. Set it with PUT /task/estimate/{id}.

isRecurring.description: True while the task repeats (it holds the series' repeat rule).

TaskAssignee.description: A task assignee: the user id, display name and avatar URL.

metadata.description: Provider-specific payload, already parsed from the stored JSON string.

BoardPagination.description: Always paginated: 50 tasks by default, at most 100 per page. Continue through totalPages to retrieve all tasks. For each task page, follow relatedPage through relatedTotalPages to retrieve all labels, external links and columns (100 related rows per kind per request, plus up to 100 columns needed to represent the tasks).

descriptionDeferred.description: True when a project description above 64 KiB is omitted; use project detail or public project description pages for full text.

archivedTasks.description: Archived tasks of any column, planned included; they appear nowhere else.

plannedTasks.description: Planned tasks that are not archived.

requests.description: Effective: the switch and the project's Intake feature.

guestsAllowed.description: Effective: the switch and the server's guest access.

assignees.description: Only when the board shows assignees.

counts.description: Present only for features that are on.

assignees.description: Only when the board shows assignees.

value.description: 1 for up, -1 for down.

boardTaskNumber.description: The accepted task, or the duplicate target, when it is on this board.

title.description: May be empty (Untitled).

content.description: The page as editor JSON, rebuilt from an allowlist. Mentions, task links, file cards and links to unpublished pages are `redacted` nodes ({ kind }); a link to a published page carries its token and title. Images are the page's own uploads served through this link, or web images.

hasSamlSignIn.description: An identity provider is connected for SAML sign-in, so the sign-in screen offers it.

exportRetentionDays.description: Days a finished task export stays downloadable.

instanceName.description: The instance's display name, shown on the sign-in screen and on public boards.

customOAuthButtonLabel.description: Label of the custom OAuth sign-in button, or null for the default copy.

publicBoardsEnabled.description: Whether public boards are allowed on this instance. When false every public link answers 404.

passwordResetEnabled.description: Whether the sign-in screen offers a forgotten-password link: password sign-in is on and outgoing email is configured.

publicLandingEnabled.description: Whether signed-out visitors to the web app's root see the product landing page. When false they go straight to sign-in.

passwordSignUpForInvitations.description: Password sign-up is off, but people with a valid invitation may still create a password account.

requiredSignInProvider.description: Everyone signs in through this provider; instance admins keep password sign-in. Null when there is no requirement.

requireTwoFactor.description: Accounts that can sign in with a password must set up two-factor before they can use anything. Email links and codes are turned off.

sourceCodeUrl.description: Where people using this instance can get its source code, as the AGPL-3.0 requires: MARGAYA_SOURCE_URL, or the official repository.

redirect.description: Where to send the browser next: back to the client with a code on approval, or with an error on denial.

idToken.description: The stored id_token for the user's `custom` OAuth account, or null when they have no such account.

dueDate.description: The soonest due date among the project's open, non-archived tasks.

ProjectStatistics.description: completionPercentage is (completed + archived open tasks) / (tasks - cancelled), rounded; 0 with no tasks and 100 when every task is cancelled. Archived tasks keep their column's group. Triage tasks are not counted.

slug.description: Short prefix used in task identifiers, e.g. KAN-12.

isPublic.description: When true the project's board is readable without signing in, via /api/public-project/{id}.

archivedAt.description: Non-null once archived; archived projects are hidden by default.

lastTaskNumber.description: Highest task number issued in this project; the next task gets this plus one.

cyclesEnabled.description: Whether Cycles is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

modulesEnabled.description: Whether Modules is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

viewsEnabled.description: Whether Project views is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

pagesEnabled.description: Whether Pages is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

intakeEnabled.description: Whether Intake is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

estimatesEnabled.description: Whether Estimates is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

timeTrackingEnabled.description: Whether Time tracking is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

aiEnabled.description: Whether AI (effective only while the instance and the workspace have AI on) is turned on. While off, its routes answer 403 and its data is kept.

leadUserId.description: The project lead, a workspace member; null when none. Cleared when the member leaves the workspace.

visibility.description: open: reached through workspace roles. restricted: only by its project members, and by workspace owners and admins; anyone else gets 404.

defaultAssigneeUserId.description: Assigned to new tasks created without assignees (API create with no assignee field, intake accept, and as a prefill in the web create flows); null when none. Cleared when the member leaves the workspace.

projectRole.description: The project role that caps your rights there.

statements.description: What that project role grants, as resource to actions. You may do there what both it and your workspace role grant.

canManage.description: Whether the caller may change visibility and members (project:share, or the project lead).

role.description: Project role: a workspace role name that caps the member's rights in a restricted project.

key.description: The task key (WEB-12).

SimilarTasks.description: Up to five open tasks of the project like the typed title (full-text ranked), best match first.

userId.description: The first assignee, or null. Mirrors `assigneeIds[0]`.

assigneeIds.description: Every assignee's user id, first assignee first.

descriptionDeferred.description: True when the list omits a large description; load the task detail or description pages to read it. Do not replace stored text with this null summary.

status.description: The slug of the column the task sits in, or planned. Archived tasks keep theirs; see archivedAt.

priority.description: One of: no-priority, low, medium, high, urgent.

isMilestone.description: True when the task marks one date; the timeline draws it on its due date. Set it with PUT /task/milestone/{id}.

completedAt.description: When the task entered a completed-group column; null while it is not completed. Archiving never changes it.

estimatePointId.description: Point of the project's active estimate system, or null. Resolve its value with GET /estimate/{projectId}. Set it with PUT /task/estimate/{id}.

archivedAt.description: When the task was archived; null while it is not. An archived task keeps its column (status).

createdBy.description: The user who created the task; null for tasks made by integrations or whose creator was deleted.

cycleId.description: The cycle the task is planned in, or null. Always null while the project's cycles feature is off.

key.description: The canonical key, in upper case (WEB-12).

archivedAt.description: Set when the task is archived; its status is its column.

userId.description: The first assignee, or null.

assigneeIds.description: Every assignee's user id, first assignee first.

labels.description: Label names and colors, without their ids.

tasks.description: Per-task outcome, each carrying a success flag.

authorId.description: Who saved it. Null for the text the task had before its history began, and for deleted users.

savedAt.description: The latest save in this version: saves by the same person within 10 minutes share one version.

size.description: Length of the description in characters.

preview.description: The start of the description as plain text.

authorId.description: Who saved it. Null for the text the task had before its history began, and for deleted users.

savedAt.description: The latest save in this version: saves by the same person within 10 minutes share one version.

size.description: Length of the description in characters.

key.description: Object key to send back to the finalize route.

uploadUrl.description: Presigned URL to PUT the image bytes to.

headers.description: Headers that must accompany the upload request, including Content-Type.

url.description: Where the stored image can be read back from.

slug.description: Stable identifier derived from the name; tasks store this as their status.

position.description: Board order, ascending. Columns are always returned sorted by it.

isFinal.description: True exactly when the group is completed or cancelled. Maintained by the API; it stops overdue reminders for tasks in the column.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last page.

key.description: e.g. WEB-12

type.description: One of: comment, task, create, status_changed, priority_changed, assignee_changed, unassigned, due_date_changed, title_changed, description_changed, cycle_changed, module_added, module_removed, estimate_changed, start_date_changed, label_added, label_removed, relation_added, relation_removed, parent_changed, subtask_added, subtask_removed, link_added, link_updated, link_removed, attachment_added, attachment_removed, copied_from, copied_to, archived, unarchived, recurrence_set, recurrence_removed, recurred_from, recurred_to.Assignee rows are per person: assignee_changed carries newAssigneeId, newAssignee (name) and isSelfAssigned in eventData; unassigned carries oldAssigneeId, oldAssignee (name) and isSelfUnassigned (older unassigned rows have no eventData and mean the whole task was unassigned). cycle_changed carries oldCycleId, oldCycleName, oldCycleProjectId, newCycleId, newCycleName and newCycleProjectId in eventData (older rows have no project ids), plus reason=cycle_deleted when the old cycle was deleted. module_added and module_removed carry moduleId, moduleName and moduleProjectId (not on older rows), plus reason=module_deleted when the module was deleted. estimate_changed carries oldPointId, newPointId, oldValue, newValue (value text at the time, minutes for time systems) and oldType, newType (points, categories or time), plus a reason (point_deleted, system_switched, system_deleted or task_moved) when it was not a direct edit. Task-detail types keep snapshots so they stay readable after renames and deletes; a task reference is { id, key, title, projectId }: start_date_changed carries oldStartDate and newStartDate (ISO or null); label_added and label_removed carry name and color; description_changed carries nothing (saves by the same person within 10 minutes share one row); relation_added and relation_removed are written on both tasks and carry relation (the key from that task's side: blocked_by, blocking, related, duplicate, start_before, start_after, finish_before or finish_after), otherTaskId, otherTaskKey, otherTaskTitle and otherProjectId; parent_changed carries oldParent and newParent (task references or null); subtask_added and subtask_removed (on the parent) carry otherTaskId, otherTaskKey, otherTaskTitle and otherProjectId of the sub-task; link_added, link_updated and link_removed carry linkId, url, title and host (link_updated also oldUrl and oldTitle); attachment_added and attachment_removed carry attachmentId, filename, size and mimeType; copied_from (on the copy) carries sourceTaskId, sourceTaskKey, sourceTaskTitle, sourceProjectId and included (option keys); copied_to (on the source) carries copyTaskId, copyTaskKey, copyTaskTitle and copyProjectId. recurrence_set and recurrence_removed carry the repeat rule (frequency, interval, weekdays, monthDay, trigger, endDate, maxOccurrences; recurrence_set also updated); recurred_from (on a repeating task's next instance) carries sourceTaskId, sourceTaskKey, sourceTaskTitle, projectId, date and reason (completion or schedule); recurred_to (on the instance before it) carries nextTaskId, nextTaskKey, nextTaskTitle, projectId, date and reason. moved carries fromProjectId, fromProjectName, oldStatus, toProjectId, toProjectName and newStatus.

eventData.description: Type-specific payload, e.g. { oldStatus, newStatus } for status_changed. Null for plain comments. A snapshot naming a project the caller can't see (or one that no longer exists in this workspace) is redacted when read: its fields are null and a flag says so, and search neither matches nor shows it. The flags are otherTaskHidden (relations and sub-tasks), sourceTaskHidden (copied_from, recurred_from), copyTaskHidden (copied_to), nextTaskHidden (recurred_to), fromProjectHidden and toProjectHidden (moved, which also blanks that side's status), hidden inside oldParent, newParent or automation (parent_changed, and the rule of a row a rule wrote), oldCycleHidden and newCycleHidden (cycle_changed), moduleHidden (module_added, module_removed), copiedFromHidden (create), and for rows written before the task left that project statusHidden (status_changed), columnHidden (intake_accepted) and duplicateHidden (intake_duplicate). A client should present these as another project, not as missing data.

externalUserName.description: Set when the activity was imported from another tool.

externalSource.description: The tool it was imported from: jira, trello, linear, asana or github.

visibility.description: Comments only: public comments also show on the project's public board. Everything else is internal.

parentId.description: Comments only: the top-level comment this one replies to, or null. Threads are one level deep; deleting a comment turns its replies into top-level comments.

userId.description: The author, or null when their account was deleted.

visibility.description: public comments also show on the public board.

parentId.description: The top-level comment this one replies to, or null for a top-level comment. Threads are one level deep; deleting a comment turns its replies into top-level comments.

user.description: The author, or null when their account (a person or an agent) was deleted; the comment stays.

isGuest.description: A guest (anonymous) account from a public board.

entry.description: Null when no timer is running.

timeZone.description: The zone whose local days the range was read in.

runningCount.description: Entries still running. Their time is not in any total until they stop.

userId.description: Null for time logged by people no longer in the workspace, counted together.
Null once the user who logged the time has been removed.

endTime.description: Null while the timer is still running.

duration.description: Elapsed seconds, filled in once the entry has an endTime.

stoppedEntries.description: The caller's running entries that this one stopped. Empty unless the new entry is itself running.

content.description: Free-text body. Null for generated notifications, whose text the client renders from type and eventData.

type.description: One of: info, task_created, workspace_created, task_status_changed, task_assignee_changed, time_entry_created, due_date_reminder, task_overdue, task_mention, task_comment, task_updated, intake_accepted, intake_declined, intake_duplicate, page_mention, page_comment, page_updated, automation_notice (an automation rule's notify action; eventData.ruleName, eventData.message).

eventData.description: Type-specific payload. Task notifications carry { taskTitle, taskKey, projectId, workspaceId, actorName }, plus { oldStatus, newStatus } for status changes, { commenterName, commentId, commentPreview } for comments, { mentionerName, source, commentId, commentPreview } for mentions, { field, oldValue, newValue } for task_updated (field is priority, dueDate or title), { leadTimeMinutes, dueDate, dueDay } for reminders (dueDay is the due date's day in the recipient's time zone), { pageTitle, mentionerName, projectId, workspaceId } for page_mention, { pageTitle, commenterName, commentId, commentPreview, projectId, workspaceId } for page_comment, and { pageTitle, editorName, projectId, workspaceId } for page_updated (all resourceType page).

resourceId.description: The id of the task or workspace the notification points at.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the notification belongs to, derived from its resource. Null for notifications without a resource, which show in every workspace's inbox.

actorId.description: Who caused it. Null for system notifications (reminders) and integration changes.

snoozedUntil.description: Snoozed until this instant; hidden from the Inbox view.

resurfacedAt.description: When a snooze ended; the Inbox view orders by this, else createdAt.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page with the same view; null on the last page.

actor.description: Who caused it; never includes an email.

task.description: The notification's task, read fresh (current title). Null for non-task notifications and deleted tasks.

sortAt.description: The instant the current view orders by: resurfacedAt or createdAt (inbox), snoozedUntil (snoozed), archivedAt (archived).

isSnoozed.description: True while snoozedUntil is in the future.

unread.description: Unread notifications in the Inbox view, every type.

unreadMentions.description: Unread mentions in the Inbox view.

updatedCount.description: How many notifications were changed or deleted.

available.description: False until the instance sets VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY and VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY.

publicKey.description: The key browsers subscribe with, when push is available.

endpoint.description: Lets a browser recognize its own entry in the list.

taskUpdateEnabled.description: Priority, due date and title changes on tasks you are assigned to or subscribed to.

dueDateReminderLeadTimeMinutes.description: How long before a due date the reminder fires, in minutes.

digestWeekday.description: The weekly digest's day, 0 = Sunday to 6 = Saturday.

digestHour.description: The local hour (0-23) digests are sent.

lastDigestSentAt.description: When the last digest period was handled.

workspaces.description: Per-workspace overrides. A workspace with no rule follows the global settings.

isActive.description: Turn all notifications for this workspace on or off.

pushEnabled.description: Whether your devices get push for this workspace. A workspace with no rule does.

projectMode.description: `all` notifies for every project in the workspace; `selected` restricts it to selectedProjectIds.

totalCount.description: Total matches found before the `limit` slice, so a caller can tell that more exist.

content.description: Matched body text, for comment and activity results. Activities get a rendered summary such as `changed status from Todo to In Progress`; a task in a project the caller can't see reads `a task in another project`. Pages get a snippet of about 160 characters around the first match.

relevanceScore.description: Higher is a better match: 10 for an exact task key (WEB-12), 3 when the whole query matches the title, 2 for a body match, each plus a full-text rank below 1. Results are sorted by score, then by createdAt descending.

taskNumber.description: For task, comment, activity and intake results: the number in the task key.

taskId.description: For comment and activity results: the task they belong to.

status.description: A task's column slug, a module's status, or an intake request's effective status.

text.description: Plain text around the best matches: up to two fragments joined by ` … `.

highlights.description: Matched spans of `text`, as [start, end) offsets in UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string indices).

SearchSnippet.description: For task, comment and page results: highlighted body text around the match.

appName.description: The configured GitHub App slug, or null when this instance has no App set up.

repositories.description: Deduplicated across installations, most recently updated first.

installation_id.description: Which App installation this repository came through.

repositories.description: Full names of the repositories under this installation. Empty when listing them failed.

permissions.description: The permissions the installation currently grants.

missingPermissions.description: Permissions that must be granted before the link will work.

message.description: A human-readable summary to show the user.

settingsUrl.description: Where to adjust the installation, when one exists.

installationUrl.description: Where to install the App, when it is not installed yet.

installationId.description: The GitHub App installation that grants access to the repository.

branchPattern.description: Template used to name branches created for a task.

commentTaskLinkOnGitHubIssue.description: When on, Margaya comments a link back to the task on the linked GitHub issue.

skipped.description: Issues whose linked task or source disappeared or belongs to another project.

installationId.description: The GitHub App installation that grants access to the repository.

branchPattern.description: Template used to name branches created for a task.

commentTaskLinkOnGitHubIssue.description: When on, Margaya comments a link back to the task on the linked GitHub issue.

message.description: A human-readable summary to show the user.

failureReason.description: Why verification failed, when it did. `redirected` usually means the base URL is behind a proxy that rewrites it.

baseUrl.description: Root URL of the Gitea instance.

webhookUrl.description: Where Gitea should POST events for this project.

webhookSecret.description: Only returned to callers with workspace:manage_settings, so the value can be pasted into Gitea.

commentTaskLinkOnGiteaIssue.description: When on, Margaya comments a link back to the task on the linked Gitea issue.

updated.description: Existing tasks that were refreshed from their issue.

maskedSecret.description: A preview of the HMAC signing secret used to sign outgoing deliveries.

dueDateReminderLeadTimeMinutes.description: How long before a due date the dueDateReminder event fires, in minutes.

maskedWebhookUrl.description: The webhook URL with its secret path segment masked, or an empty string when none is set.
The webhook URL with its secret path segment masked, or an empty string when none is set.
The webhook URL with its secret path segment masked, or an empty string when none is set.

chatId.description: The Telegram chat, group, or channel messages are sent to.

threadId.description: Forum topic id, when the target group uses topics.

chatLabel.description: A human-readable name for the chat, shown in the UI.

projectSlug.description: The task's own project key, for {projectSlug}-{number}.

group.description: The task's status group (backlog for planned tasks). Archived tasks keep their column's group.

userId.description: The first assignee, or null.

assigneeIds.description: Every assignee's user id, first assignee first.

relationType.description: The stored type, source → target: `subtask` (source is the parent), `blocks` (source blocks target), `related`, `duplicate` (source is a duplicate of target), `start_before` (source starts before target) or `finish_before` (source finishes before target). Each task reads it from its own side: blocks is blocking for the source and blocked_by for the target, start_before becomes start_after and finish_before becomes finish_after for the target.

truncated.description: True when the project holds more dependencies than one response carries; the oldest are returned.

blockedTaskIds.description: The project's open tasks that an open task still blocks, wherever the blocker lives. Being blocked never stops a status change.

relationType.description: `blocks` (source must finish before target starts), `start_before` (source starts before target) or `finish_before` (source finishes before target).

allOf.description: The task's parent after the change, or null.

host.description: The URL's host without a leading www. (punycode for international names), shown so a title can't hide the destination.

TaskLinkCreator.description: Null when the user was deleted.

mimeType.description: The content type storage reported for the uploaded file.

kind.description: image for the image types shown inline, attachment otherwise.

url.description: GET /asset/{id}: images open inline, every other type downloads. Never readable without signing in, even on a public project.

downloadUrl.description: The same URL with ?download=1, which always downloads.

createdBy.description: Who uploaded it; null when the user was deleted.

key.description: The copy's task key, e.g. WEB-13.

skipped.description: Requested options the source had data for that could not be copied, e.g. parent or planning across projects, planning while the feature is off, or assignees when all of them left the workspace.

TaskTemplate.description: Defaults for a new task. References that went stale (a deleted label or column, a member who left, a point outside the active estimate system) are left out.

name.description: Unique in the project, case-insensitively.

titlePattern.description: The new task's title. `{title}` is replaced by the typed title; without it, a typed title is appended after a space.

columnId.description: A column of this project (not the intake triage column), or null for the project's entry column.

labelIds.description: Workspace labels (not task copies) to put on the task.

assigneeIds.description: Workspace members to assign. Empty means the project's default assignee, if any.

estimatePointId.description: A point of the project's active estimate system; ignored while estimates are off.

subtasks.description: Sub-task titles, created under the new task in this order (needs task:update to use).

assigneeIds.description: Workspace members to assign. Empty means the project's default assignee, if any.

estimatePointId.description: A point of the project's active estimate system; ignored while estimates are off.

subtasks.description: Sub-task titles, created under the new task in this order (needs task:update to use).

UpdateTaskTemplateBody.description: Any subset of the template's fields.

title.description: Typed title, merged into the title pattern.

status.description: A column slug that overrides the template's column, e.g. the column a quick add ran in.

taskId.description: The series' current instance, which holds the rule.

weekdays.description: Weekly: the days it repeats on (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday). Empty for other frequencies.

monthDay.description: Monthly and yearly: the day of the month.

anchorDate.description: The current instance's occurrence date in the workspace's time zone; the pattern counts from it.

endDate.description: Last day an instance may fall on.

occurrenceCount.description: Instances so far, the first task included.

nextDate.description: The next instance's date: when the schedule creates it, or the date it gets if this one is completed today. Null once the series has ended.

TaskRecurrence.description: The task's repeat rule, or null when it does not repeat.

interval.description: Every this many days, weeks, months or years. Defaults to 1.

weekdays.description: Weekly only: the days it repeats on, 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday. Defaults to the weekday of the task's date.

monthDay.description: Monthly and yearly only: the day of the month, clamped to shorter months. Defaults to the day of the task's date.

trigger.description: completion (default): the next instance is created when this one is completed. schedule: it is created on its date, in the workspace's time zone, whether or not this one is done.

endDate.description: Last day an instance may fall on (inclusive). Leave out or null for no end date.

maxOccurrences.description: Total number of instances, this task included. Leave out or null for no limit. Not together with endDate.

columns.description: Detected CSV columns; count is how many columns repeat the name (Labels, Comment, Sprint…).

suggestedStatus.description: Column slug, or `planned` for the backlog.

name.description: As the export writes it.

member.description: The matched workspace member, or null.

alreadyImported.description: Issues whose key was imported into this project before.

estimates.description: Estimates are on and the active system takes Jira values (points or time).

skipped.description: Issues imported before and left as they are.

unmatchedPeople.description: Assignees and reporters with no matching workspace member; their issues stay unassigned.

columns.description: Detected CSV columns, or the Trello lists cards are on, with counts.

suggestedStatus.description: Column slug, or `planned` for the backlog.

name.description: As the export writes it.

member.description: The workspace member matched by email (or unique name), or null: their items stay unassigned with a note.

alreadyImported.description: Items imported into this project before.

skipped.description: Items imported before and left as they are.

relations.description: Sub-task, blocking and related relations added.

unmatchedPeople.description: Assignees with no matching workspace member; their items stay unassigned with a note in the description.

resourceType.description: The kind of remote resource, e.g. `issue` or `pull_request`.

externalId.description: The provider's own identifier for the linked resource.

metadata.description: Provider-specific payload, parsed from the stored JSON string. Null when the link has no metadata.

integrationType.description: The integration that emits the event, e.g. `github`.

eventType.description: The provider event that triggers the move, e.g. `pull_request.opened`.

columnId.description: The column tasks are moved to when the event fires.

status.description: Always `pending` here; expired and accepted ones are filtered out.

valid.description: True only when the invitation can still be accepted.

invitation.description: Omitted when the invitation does not exist, was already accepted, or was canceled -- the details are withheld rather than leaked.

error.description: Why the invitation is unusable, when valid is false.

teamId.description: Deprecated: invitations no longer target a team, and new ones leave it null. Kept so older clients still parse the response; don't rely on it.

role.description: The role the invitation grants: viewer, member, admin, guest (only the projects they are added to) or one of the workspace's custom roles.
The project role: viewer, member, admin or one of the workspace's custom roles. For a guest it caps their rights in that project, which never go beyond the Guest role.

projects.description: The projects the invitee joins on acceptance, replacing the current list; an empty list clears it. At most 50.

timezone.description: The workspace's IANA time zone. Existing workspaces start on UTC.

allowPublicPages.description: Whether pages may be published to a read-only public link. Off by default; turning it off revokes every published page link.

hasPassword.description: Whether the account can sign in with a password (and so change it).

twoFactorEnabled.description: Whether password sign-in asks for an authenticator code (TOTP).

twoFactorRequired.description: Whether this server requires two-factor of this account. If it isn't on yet, every other request answers 403 with code TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED until it is.

sessions.description: Active sessions, most recently active first.

userAgent.description: The browser's user agent when the session started.

ipAddress.description: The client IP when the session started, if known.

lastActiveAt.description: When the session was last refreshed. Sessions refresh about once a day of use, so this is approximate.

current.description: True for the session that made this request.

projectId.description: The project the entity lives in (the entity itself for projects).

position.description: Display order, ascending. New favorites go on top.

name.description: Project name, task title, cycle name, and so on.

key.description: Task: the project key and number, e.g. "web-12" (display it uppercased). Project: its key. Others: null.

isArchived.description: The entity or its project is archived.

feature.description: The project feature that gates the entity (cycles, modules, views, pages), or null.

details.description: Type-specific extras. Task: group, priority, assigneeId (the first assignee), assigneeIds (every assignee, first first) and status.

visitedAt.description: The most recent visit; lists are ordered by it, newest first.

today.description: The server's UTC date the status was derived from.

isFrozen.description: True once unfinished tasks were transferred out; counts and progress then come from the report frozen at that moment.

progress.description: Percent done, 0–100: completed ÷ (total − cancelled), rounded. 0 without tasks, 100 when every task is cancelled.

rollover.description: What the project's cycle auto-rollover did when this cycle ended; null until it ran (or while it is off).

CycleStatus.description: Derived from the dates against the server's UTC today: draft (no dates), upcoming (starts after today), current (today is inside the inclusive range), completed (ended before today). Archived cycles are always completed.

CycleCounts.description: Visible member tasks (not archived, not in triage) per column group.

unchanged.description: Already in this cycle (add), or not in it (remove).

ignored.description: Not a visible task of the cycle's project. Not an error, so repeated bulk calls stay safe.

allOf.description: The chart in points mode: every number sums estimate values (minutes for time systems) instead of counting tasks, and tasks without an estimate weigh 0. Null unless a numeric system is active and the cycle has dates and estimated tasks.

CycleChart.description: Burn-down and burn-up data over every day of the cycle. Null for drafts and when no task is in scope.

remaining.description: Scope minus tasks completed by that day; null after today.

completed.description: Tasks completed by that day; null after today.

ideal.description: The straight burn-down line from scope to 0.

userId.description: Null for unassigned tasks (listed last). A task with several assignees counts in each of their rows.

name.description: Null for tasks without labels (listed last). A task with several labels counts in each.

enabled.description: True when the project's estimates feature is on and a system is active. When false, every count is 0, every sum is null and distribution is empty.

isNumeric.description: True for points and time systems. Show sums only then; otherwise fall back to task counts.

taskCount.description: Visible tasks in scope (not archived, not in triage). Cancelled tasks are included.

total.description: Sum of the values over the scope, rounded to 2 decimals (minutes for time). 0 when nothing is estimated; null for categories.

completed.description: The same sum over the completed group.

distribution.description: One row per value of the active system in position order, zero counts included.

EstimateTotals.description: Estimate totals over the same tasks. enabled is false while the project's estimates feature is off or no system is active. Null only for a report frozen before estimates existed.

total.description: Sum of the values; null unless the system is numeric.

position.description: Manual order, ascending; new modules go first.

progress.description: Percent done, 0–100: completed ÷ (total − cancelled), rounded. 0 without tasks, 100 when every task is cancelled.

ModuleStatus.description: Set by hand: backlog, planned, in-progress, paused, completed or cancelled.

ModuleCounts.description: Visible member tasks (not archived, not in triage) per column group.

members.description: Ordered by name. Users who left the workspace are still listed.

removedTaskIds.description: The tasks the module held; they stay in the project.

today.description: The server's UTC date the chart was computed against.

allOf.description: Estimate totals over the same tasks. enabled is false while the project's estimates feature is off or no system is active.

completed.description: Tasks completed by that day; null after today.

ideal.description: The straight burn-down line from scope to 0.

name.description: Null for tasks without labels (listed last). A task with several labels counts in each.

unchanged.description: Already in this module (add), or not in it (remove).

ignored.description: Not a visible task of the module's project. Not an error, so repeated bulk calls stay safe.

estimates.description: The active system first, then the others, newest first.

isActive.description: At most one system per project is active; tasks only use its values.

value.description: Canonical display text. Time systems hold whole minutes, for example "90".

numericValue.description: The value as a number (minutes for time); null for categories.

position.description: 1..n within the system, the sort order. Points and time are ordered by value.

taskCount.description: Tasks on this value right now, archived ones included.

clearedTaskCount.description: Tasks left without an estimate (active systems only).

previousEstimateId.description: The system that was active before the call; the target itself when it already was.

remappedTaskCount.description: Tasks moved to a value of the new system.

fromPointId.description: A value of the currently active system.

toPointId.description: A value of the system being activated, or null for no estimate.

total.description: Requests matching every filter, the tab included.

projectId.description: The project whose queue the request was submitted to.

snoozedUntil.description: Set only while the request is snoozed.

resolutionNote.description: The reason given when declining or marking a duplicate.

allOf.description: Who made the latest triage decision.

hasMoreGroups.description: More than 100 groups: the rest carry counts, not rows.

tasks.description: Task id to row; a task in several groups appears once.

subGroups.description: Cells of the group when sub-grouped; rows live there.

key.description: Project key and number: WEB-12.

Date `in`: presets today, yesterday, tomorrow, thisWeek, lastWeek, nextWeek, thisMonth, lastMonth, nextMonth, past, future, none. At most 100 values of at most 128 characters.

fieldId.description: The custom field, for customField only.

groupBy.description: A built-in key, or customField:<field id> to group by a custom field's value. status needs exactly one project in scope. Ignored in ids mode.

field.description: A built-in field, or customField:<field id> to sort by a custom field's value.

direction.description: Defaults per field: asc for manual, startDate, dueDate, title, number, status, assignee, label, cycle, module and custom fields; desc for the rest (archivedAt included). Nulls always come last.

limit.description: Rows per group (per cell when sub-grouped). Default 50.

subGroup.description: With group: load the next slice of this cell only.

timeZone.description: IANA zone that date filters and `today` use. Default UTC.

subscribed.description: The effective state: a subscription, or an assignment the caller has not unsubscribed from.

reason.description: Why the caller is subscribed (creator, assignee, commenter, mention or manual); null when not subscribed.

isMuted.description: The caller explicitly unsubscribed. Mentions and new assignments still notify, and subscribe again.

subscriberCount.description: Distinct watchers: subscribed users plus assignees, minus those who unsubscribed.

task.description: Reactions on the task itself, ordered by each emoji's first use.

reacted.description: The current user has this reaction.

users.description: Who reacted, earliest first, at most 10.

at.description: When the rule would have fired (ISO time): the integration event, the moment the task crossed the months threshold, or the cycle's end.

outcome.description: change: the task would have changed (for an automation rule: the trigger and the conditions match); unchanged: it was already there; skipped: the engine leaves it alone (a final column, no next cycle, or the task does not meet the automation rule's conditions).

notes.description: Caveats: the integration is not connected; only each branch's last push is known; archive and close replay from each task's last update; flow alerts only notify; the rule turns nothing on; or an automation rule's conditions were checked against each task as it is now.

projectId.description: The project whose history is replayed.

days.description: How many days of history to replay, 1-90.

outcome.description: success: every action applied or had nothing to change; partial: some failed; failed: all failed; skipped: the loop guard (LOOP_DEPTH) or the per-task rate limit (RATE_LIMITED) stopped it.

name.description: What the rule is for, shown in the list.

status.description: same_language: the content is already in the reader's language; text is null.

sourceLanguage.description: ISO 639-1 code of the original, when it could be told.

text.description: The translation (Markdown for comments and descriptions).

cached.description: Served from the cache: the same text was translated for this language before.

kind.description: What to translate: a comment, a task's description or a page's content.

id.description: The comment (activity), task or page ID.

targetLocale.description: The reader's language, such as de-DE. Default: the language saved in the caller's profile.

since.description: Changes are counted from here: the previous shared brief, else 7 days ago.

probabilityByEnd.description: Percent chance to finish by the end date.

previous.description: The last shared brief, for the diff.

scopeId.description: The cycle, module or project ID.

audience.description: team: concrete; leadership: outcomes and risks first; client: customer-safe (no people, no internal process; not for restricted projects).

locale.description: The caller's UI language; the answer is written in it. Defaults to the language saved in the caller's profile.

pageId.description: The Page the brief was saved as (same project). Omit when it was copied.

status.description: no_estimate: estimates are off or no system is active; insufficient_history: fewer than 3 similar completed and estimated tasks.

share.description: Share (0..1) of the similar tasks' weight on this value.

cycleTime.description: Actual cycle time (first start to completion) of the similar tasks.

unmeasured.description: Completed, estimated tasks without a visible start (no cycle time).

ordered.description: Whether bigger estimates really took longer (medians of buckets with 3+ samples never go down); null with fewer than two such buckets.

basis.description: cycles: up to 6 ended cycles of the project (2 needed); throughput: tasks completed in every window of the cycle's length over the last 56 days; none: not enough history or no dates.

percent.description: Load as a percent of a usual cycle (the median).

deferrals.description: Not-started tasks to move out until the load fits: lowest priority, then fewest dependants first.

members.description: Load per assignee against what they usually finished in a cycle; only for people with cycle:update, otherwise null.

CapacityRange.description: What comparable time held before: 25th percentile, median and 75th percentile.

sayDoPercent.description: Percent of the work committed at the start that was done.

hiddenBlockers.description: Blockers in projects you can't see (counted, not named). Through a project-limited API key, those outside its projects are left out altogether.

p85.description: The 85% date of the earliest shared stakeholder brief of the cycle.

projectId.description: Project ID

title.description: The title to match when the task does not exist yet (or to override its title).

outputSummary.description: The agent's closing summary. change.description: The change-set entry of a write: op, the task, and before and after values.

text.description: What the model wrote in a model step; null unless the instance stores prompts (ai.retention.storePrompts).

links.description: App paths of the task a change touched and of what it created, edited or linked (a page, a sub-task, the other task); null when none.

shared.description: Shared with the workspace; otherwise personal.

ownerId.description: The person a personal connector belongs to.

url.description: Only for people who may change the connector (its owner, or ai:manage for shared ones).

secretLast4.description: The secret's last four characters, for people who may change the connector. The secret itself is never returned.

Send the version from the first page with each later one: if the task was edited in between, the answer is 409 and the read starts again from offset 0. Works without signing in.

patch.description: Apply one operation to many tasks at once. Every task must be in the same workspace; updateEstimate also needs them in one project with its Estimates feature on. The assignee operations (updateAssignee, addAssignee, removeAssignee) need task:assign and change every task in one transaction; their updatedCount counts the tasks whose assignees actually changed. archive and unarchive (task:update) count the tasks whose archive state changed. move (task:update on every source project and on the destination) changes every task in one transaction and counts the tasks that moved.

operation.description: updateAssignee replaces every task's assignees with one user (null clears them); addAssignee and removeAssignee add or remove one user and keep the others. archive and unarchive archive or restore the tasks in their columns; updateStatus with the value archived is an alias of archive, and updateStatus with a column restores archived tasks. move sends the tasks to another project of the workspace, all or none: they get new task keys, keep their status when the destination has it and otherwise take its first column, and leave their cycle, modules and estimate. Labels and assignees stay. A custom field value follows to a destination field of the same name and type, and is removed when there is none. Tasks already in the destination are skipped.

value.description: The new value for the chosen operation. Unused by `delete`, `archive` and `unarchive`; null clears the assignees (updateAssignee), a due or start date, or an estimate; updateStartDate is refused when the date falls after a selected task's due date; a user id for addAssignee and removeAssignee. updateEstimate takes a point of the project's active estimate system and needs every task in one project. move takes the destination project's id.

post.description: Add a task to a project. It is placed in the column named by `status`; the legacy status `archived` creates it archived in the project's entry column. When the body has neither field, the project's default assignee (if set) is assigned; send `assigneeIds: []` to create the task unassigned. The caller is recorded as the task's creator. With `parentId` the task is created as that task's subtask in one transaction, which also needs task:update.

get.description: Search across tasks, projects, workspaces, comments, activities, pages, cycles, modules, saved views and intake requests in one workspace. Pages need page:read and appear only when public or the caller's own, not archived, in projects with Pages on. Cycles, modules and views need cycle:read, module:read and view:read; archived cycles and modules, other people's private views, and projects with the feature off are left out. Intake requests not yet accepted appear with intake:read, or only the caller's own with intake:create alone. Matching is PostgreSQL full-text search: `q` takes web-search syntax ("quoted phrases", `or`, `-exclude`), the last word also matches as a prefix, and accents are ignored where the server supports it. A whole-query task key such as `WEB-12` ranks first. Chinese, Japanese and Thai text also matches by substring. Results are ranked by relevance and returned as a single flat list, each entry tagged with its `type`; task, comment and page results carry a highlighted `snippet`. An activity is never matched or described by what it says about a project the caller can't see.

post.description: Counts tasks (or sums estimate points or a number custom field) by an x-axis dimension, optionally segmented by a second category dimension, over the task set that the task query filters describe. Buckets come in the dimension's natural order with none last (a dropdown custom field: its option order, removed options still on tasks after them); dates are bucketed by week or month in context.timeZone and zero-filled. At most 50 category buckets (120 date buckets, the most recent) are returned; segments beyond the top 5 (8 for labels) fold into `other`, whose cells are sums. A charted custom field must belong to a scope project the caller can see. Totals count distinct tasks: a task with several assignees, labels or modules counts once in each of their buckets, so buckets (and stacked cells) can sum to more than the total. `none` is the bucket of tasks without a value, and a feature that is off in a project reads as none (points as 0). Archived tasks are left out unless archived is include or only; triage tasks never count. Completion % is completed ÷ (all − cancelled).

post.description: Answer a question about the workspace in plain language, in the caller's language, from tasks, pages and comments they can see (full-text search plus structured task filters such as overdue, mine, completed, blocking, a cycle or an assignee named in the question: workspace members match by full or first name, agents by full name). Questions about someone's tasks look at open work and fall back to finished work when nothing is open. Live task data comes before pages, which may be outdated. A follow-up that names nothing itself ("and its description?") is about the tasks the previous answer in `history` cited. `context` items ("@" mentions) are loaded first; `attachments` add images (for vision models) or text files; `webSearch` adds web results cited as [W:n] (only the question goes to the search provider); Margaya's own documentation is searched too, so questions about using Margaya are answered from the guides and cited as [D:n]; `skillId` adds a saved skill's prompt as the person's instructions; the workspace's memory notes are background. Restricted projects are left out unless the workspace includes them, and projects with AI off never are. The answer cites sources as [T:WEB-12], [P:<page title>], [C:<task key>/<comment id prefix>], [W:<n>] or [D:<n>]; `sources` lists what it may cite. Counting, breakdown, trend and chart questions (how many, by status, priority, assignee, label, cycle or module, created vs completed per week or day, burn-up, a chart or graph) also get live numbers computed over the tasks the caller can see, and the answer may contain a fenced ```chart block of JSON {type: bar|donut|line, title, data: [{label, value}] or series: [{name, data: [{label, value}]}], unit?} for the client to draw. `done` adds `followUps` (0-2 suggested questions, often none) and `reasoningMs`; `reasoning` events stream while the model thinks (text only when the instance shows reasoning). When nothing relevant is found, no model call is made and `noResults` is true. An answer cut off before any visible text (a reasoning model out of room) ends with an AI_PROVIDER_ERROR error event instead of an empty answer, or a 502 with the JSON fallback. Needs ai:use and AI on for the instance, the workspace and (with projectId) the project.

200.description: The answer. `meta` carries `sources` and `asOf`; `done` carries `citations`, `noResults`, `followUps` and `reasoningMs`. Streams Server-Sent Events (meta, reasoning, delta, tool_call, done or error); send Accept: application/json or ?stream=false for one JSON body instead.

schema.description: Events: meta {provider, model, tier, dataTier, destination}, reasoning {text} (the model is thinking; text only when the instance shows reasoning, else empty), delta {text}, tool_call {id, name, input}, done {stop, usage, costMicros, model, reasoningMs}, error {code, message}.

reasoningMs.description: How long the model thought before answering, in milliseconds; null when it did not think visibly.

sources.description: Everything the answer may cite, most relevant first. Only entities the caller can see and AI may read.

citations.description: The source refs the answer actually cites, in order of first use. Tokens that match no source are left out.

noResults.description: True when nothing relevant was found: no model call was made and `text` is empty; show a 'nothing found' message.

followUps.description: Zero to two short follow-up questions the person might ask next, in their language; empty unless a useful next step exists. Sent with `done`.

post.summary: Propose intake requests from a capture
post.description: Turn screenshots, key frames of a screen recording (taken in the browser; video is never uploaded) or a meeting transcript into proposed intake requests: a title, a summary, steps to reproduce, expected and actual behaviour, a suggested priority and existing labels, in the caller's language. A transcript may yield up to 10 action items, each with an owner when it names a project member. Images must be PNG, JPEG or WebP whose bytes match the declared type, at most 6 and 3.75 MB each (9 MB together); their metadata (EXIF, XMP, IPTC, text chunks) is removed before the model call. Images count as private data for routing. Nothing is created or stored. Needs ai:use and intake:create, with AI and Intake on for the project; restricted projects need the workspace to include them in AI.

post.summary: Plan changes from a chat request
post.description: Turns a request such as "create a project NX-7 with Elena as lead and three tasks" into actions to review: create_project, create_task, update_task, set_status, assign, add_comment, create_cycle, add_to_cycle, create_module, add_to_module, create_page, link_tasks, create_label, delete_task and run_agent, at most 50. Actions may point at things created earlier in the plan through temp refs. Names are resolved to ids (members, tasks by key, statuses, cycles, modules, agents) within what the caller's AI may read, and each action is checked against the caller's permissions; one that can't be applied carries a problem. An ambiguous request gets a question with options instead. Nothing changes, unless autopilot is true and the workspace allows Autopilot: then a plan without problems, questions or destructive actions is applied at once and the results come back too. Returns JSON; with Accept: text/event-stream it streams Server-Sent Events instead: context (what the plan is made from: fact counts, the items read in full with titles and links, memory notes, earlier turns), reasoning {text} while the model thinks (text only when the instance shows reasoning), then done with the plan, or error {code, message}.
